messages:
ana (CS): Mariner day0: two items blocking go-live: KMS access errors for redwood-exec role, and no events in their Splunk index. Anyone free to triage? /cc @mike @devika

deploy-bot: infra: mariner/privnet apply complete. 4 instances reporting healthy. (deploy #11012) :white_check_mark:

mike (NetOps): share the KMS error log snippet?

mariner-ops (Customer): Paste from service logs:
```
Error: AccessDeniedException: User not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:555666777888:key/aa11bb22
```

devika (Security): Usually key policy missing Redwood role ARN or an SCP deny. Please confirm the role ARN and whether the key is cross-account.

ana (CS): role they provided: `arn:aws:iam::555666777888:role/redwood-exec-prod` and they say key is in same account. They attached trimmed key policy.

ryan (CSE): Quick recommended patch: add statement with Principal = role ARN and Actions [`kms:Decrypt`,`kms:GenerateDataKey`]. Also check for explicit DENY statements or SCPs blocking KMS. I'll paste a tiny example via DM.

mariner-ops (Customer): We applied the change but still seeing decrypt errors when tasks start. Any other checks?

mike (NetOps): Another thing: if the role has a permissions boundary or session policy removing KMS actions, that can block. Can you run a policy simulator against the role for kms:Decrypt?

mariner-ops (Customer): Ran simulator -> indicates `ImplicitDeny` from role due to no Allow in IAM policy. We only added key policy.

devika (Security): Right — you need both: key policy must allow the principal, and the IAM role needs an inline/attached policy allowing kms:Decrypt/kms:GenerateDataKey. Minimal IAM policy: `{ "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"], "Effect": "Allow", "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:555666777888:key/aa11bb22" }`

mariner-ops (Customer): Added inline policy to role and re-tested service -> decrypt errors gone, inference started. Thanks.

ana (CS): Second thread: Splunk forwarding. We see no CloudWatch logs arriving. Are you running a HEC endpoint on 8088?

mariner-ops (Customer): Yes, `hec.mariner-splunk.com:8088`. curl from a web instance succeeds, but agent in priv subnet times out.

mike (NetOps): Common: NAT gateway / route table not attached to private subnet, or security group outbound is restricted. Can you run `curl -v https://hec.mariner-splunk.com:8088/services/collector/raw -H 'Authorization: Splunk <token>' -d 'ping'` from the private agent?

mariner-ops (Customer): Ran it -> timeout. NAT exists but route table for subnet-priv-c was mis-associated to an isolated rt. We'll update.

mike (NetOps): Action: Re-associate correct RT, allow outbound 443 and 8088 in SG, and add NAT gateway. ETA 60m. Assigning @mike.

mariner-ops (Customer): Re-associated RT and opened egress, re-ran curl -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK. Splunk shows our test event.

devika (Security): One more audit item: enable multi-region CloudTrail with log file validation and SSE-KMS encryption to the audit bucket. Send S3 ARN here once created. Retention default 90 days; if you need > 365 days flag procurement (renewal/pricing impact).

mariner-ops (Customer): Created trail -> s3://mariner-redwood-audit, enabled validation, used SSE-KMS with same key. Sent ARN to the team.

ryan (CSE): Final smoke: run an inference to private endpoint and verify no KMS or 5xxs. Sample command:
```
curl -X POST https://internal.mariner.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```

mariner-ops (Customer): Got 200 and event in Splunk. All green for cutover. We'll schedule monthly key rotation for dev and quarterly for prod.

ana (CS): Great. I'll check back in 7 days to confirm rotation schedule and retention. Flag renewal risk if they request > 18 months retention. Closing unless anything new. :white_check_mark:
